clue.text: Gracious old Russian leader affectionately hugging Green

indicators.note: hugging means the leader's pet name wraps around the colour word

parts.note: Gorby was the affectionate Western nickname for Mikhail Gorbachev
lime is a shade of green

explanation.surface: An old Soviet leader fondly embracing an environmentalist, to general surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gracious' is the exclamation of surprise ('Gracious me!'), not an adjective meaning kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British exclamations of astonishment; the answer is a Cockney oath from 'God blind me'.

clue.text: Shopper understands when parking's not available

indicators.note: not available means the parking letter is missing from the word for understands

parts.note: to grasp something is to understand it
P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: A shopper gets the picture when there is nowhere to park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shopper' is slang for an informer, someone who shops others to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to shop someone is to inform on them, and an informer is also called a grass.

clue.text: Area periodically leading to speed charge?

definitions.text: Area periodically leading to speed charge?

indicators.note: periodically means taking every other letter of Area, its second and fourth

parts.note: to dart is to speed
a rap is a criminal charge, as in 'take the rap'

explanation.surface: A place that from time to time results in a speeding prosecution.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer as well as building it: 'leading to' simply joins the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A police speed check set up on a stretch of road, catching motorists who then face a speeding charge.

clue.text: Repeatedly supplying ecstasy for one in Belfast club gets one fired

indicators.note: for means the letter for one is swapped out and the ecstasy letters put in its place

parts.note: Linfield is a football club in Belfast
I is the Roman numeral one
E is the usual abbreviation for the drug ecstasy, supplied here three times

explanation.surface: A Belfast club repeatedly dealing ecstasy leads to someone being sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one fired' looks like a sacked worker but means a weapon that is fired. LINFIELD is a Northern Irish football club; its I is replaced by EEE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lee-Enfield was the standard British army rifle, a weapon that is fired.

clue.text: Tips for managing one's own place abroad, largely unproductive

indicators.note: the tips are the first letters of the two words managing and one's

parts.note: to own is to have

explanation.surface: Advice for running your own home overseas, which mostly isn't paying its way.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mohave is a desert in the south-western United States, a foreign place largely barren.

clue.text: Split with this person? Perhaps once girl's old boyfriend turns up

definitions.text: Split with this person? Perhaps once

indicators.note: turns up, in a down clue, means the whole string is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Val is a girl's name, with the possessive S
a guy can be a boyfriend

explanation.surface: Breaking up with someone after an ex-boyfriend reappears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' is not a break-up but the Croatian city, once part of Yugoslavia.
explanation.definitionFit: Split is in Croatia, formerly part of Yugoslavia, so someone from there was once a Yugoslav.

clue.text: Regulars turning in quiz a drunk climber

indicators.note: turning means the picked letters are read backwards
regulars means taking every second letter along the run quiz a drunk

explanation.surface: Pub regulars at a quiz night turn on a drunken mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters U, Z, D, U, K are read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Kudzu is a fast-growing climbing vine from East Asia.

clue.text: Fail to leave Irish party after defeat by new Secretary-General

indicators.note: after places the Irish party's remainder following the knockout letters

parts.note: KO, a knockout, is a defeat

indicators.note: to leave means the word Fail departs from the party's name

parts.note: Fianna Fail is one of Ireland's main political parties
the word fail as written

explanation.surface: An Irish party is told to step aside after a fresh defeat for the UN chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fail' looks like a verb but is the last word of the party name Fianna Fail, which is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ghanaian diplomat served as UN Secretary-General from 1997 to 2006.

clue.text: Whack dipstick

definitions.meaning: a whack is a share, which in British slang is a ... (from dividend)
dipstick is slang for a fool

explanation.surface: Hit the idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses the word both for a share of the takings and for a foolish person.

clue.text: Tipping: what's ex-crossword compiler given?

definitions.meaning: tipping over means knocking over or overturning
a retired setter's setting is up, that is, over and finished

explanation.surface: Hints on a retired setter's leaving present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tipping' suggests gratuities, but it means overturning. The second half reads the answer as two words: for an ex-setter, the setting is over.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset something is to knock it over, so tipping it is the same act.

clue.text: Australian who sings a number with rapper

parts.note: Dr Dre is an American rapper

explanation.surface: An Australian singer performs a song with a rap artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Andre is an Australian-raised pop singer.

clue.text: Heartily welcomes school introducing game

indicators.note: introducing puts the school word before the game word

parts.note: a high school
fives is a handball game played in a walled court

explanation.surface: A school warmly greets the arrival of a new sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapping raised palms together is an enthusiastic gesture of greeting or celebration.

clue.text: Following row, customs finally stops check revealing underwear

indicators.note: following places the check-with-letter after the row word

parts.note: a string is a row of things such as beads

indicators.note: stops means the last letter of customs plugs a gap inside the check word

parts.note: to vet is to check

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of customs

explanation.surface: After an argument, customs officers carry out a search that exposes someone's underclothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests an argument, but it means a line of things.
explanation.definitionFit: A string vest is a mesh undershirt, a classic item of men's underclothing.

clue.text: Bag of fluid emptied completely and unfastened at the centre

indicators.note: emptied means completely loses all its inner letters, keeping only the ends
at the centre takes the middle two letters of unfastened

explanation.surface: A bag of liquid has been entirely drained and its middle undone.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyst is a sac in the body filled with fluid.

clue.text: Cold with nasty catarrh's very disturbing thing to view

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: nasty signals that the letters of catarrh's are mangled

parts.note: the letters of catarrh's, including the S

explanation.surface: A cold with horrible catarrh is a most distressing thing to see.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes television so dreadful, or a spectacle so awful, that one cannot look away.

clue.text: Figure girl might dress up for meal out

definitions.meaning: a fashion doll that a girl dresses in different outfits
Australian slang for an outdoor barbecue meal

explanation.surface: A girl dresses a doll up for a dinner out.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both the famous Mattel doll and an informal word for a barbecue.

clue.text: Restrict what can be worn in Japan, depressing the last Secretary-General

parts.note: to ban is to restrict

indicators.note: depressing, in a down clue, means one letter of the garment is pushed further down the column

parts.words: what can be worn in Japan
parts.note: a kimono is a traditional Japanese robe

explanation.surface: Limiting Japanese dress lowers the spirits of the latest UN chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depressing' looks like saddening but means lowering: the N of KIMONO drops to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The South Korean diplomat was UN Secretary-General at the time, the most recent holder of that office.

clue.text: Vodka was a killer in that company!

indicators.note: in signals that the letters lie inside the run of words vodka was a killer

explanation.surface: Drinking vodka proved fatal when in that group of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Kawasaki is a Japanese industrial corporation, famous for motorcycles.

clue.text: Sustaining an all-time high

indicators.note: high, as in intoxicated, signals the letters of an all-time are jumbled

explanation.surface: Keeping things going at a record level.
explanation.definitionFit: Alimental means nourishing, supplying food that keeps the body going.

clue.text: Careful thing to do to change, perhaps, or exclude

definitions.text: Careful thing to do to change, perhaps
definitions.meaning: one counts coins out one by one to be sure of the amount
to leave someone out of a plan

explanation.surface: Checking your change carefully, or leaving something out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to tally money out coin by coin and to exclude someone.

clue.text: Cake appearing when Christmas Ball roast's over

indicators.note: over means the three pieces together are read backwards

parts.note: Noel is another word for Christmas
O is ball-shaped
to pan is to criticise harshly, or roast

explanation.surface: A cake is served once the Christmas ball's roast dinner is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roast' suggests the Christmas dinner, but it means to criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: A napoleon is a layered pastry of puff pastry and cream, a mille-feuille.

clue.text: Cockney unable to stand grabbing cape and putting it on

indicators.note: grabbing means the Cockney word closes around the cape letter

parts.note: a Cockney drops the H of hating, which means unable to stand
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: A Londoner who can't bear it seizes a cloak and puts it on.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys famously drop their H, so 'hating' becomes 'ating.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting it on means pretending or performing, which is what acting is.

clue.text: Greeting a thing we always look up to, following with spirit

indicators.note: following puts the greeting after the abbreviation for with

parts.note: hi is a greeting

parts.words: a thing we always look up to
parts.note: the sky is always above us

explanation.surface: Saying hello to someone we admire, then having a drink with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a thing we always look up to' sounds like a hero but is literally overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisky is a distilled spirit.

clue.text: An hour after Midnight Mass interrupts prayer leader

indicators.note: interrupts means the mass letter breaks into the time

parts.note: one hour after midnight is 1 a.m., written I AM with the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: An hour after Midnight Mass begins, it is broken off by the priest.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads the prayers in a mosque.

clue.text: See 6
Looking out possible dry clothing for shaman

parts.note: on means feasible, as in 'that's not on'

indicators.note: clothing means the teetotal letters wrap around the shaman word

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means not drinking, or dry
a shaman is a healer

explanation.surface: A shaman might be dressed in something that won't get wet.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on the alert is to be watchful, keeping a lookout.

clue.text: A flavour of 1925

indicators.note: of means only a stretch from inside the two run-together answers is taken, dropping the letters around it

parts.note: the numbers refer to the answers of 19 across and 25 down, run together

explanation.surface: A taste of the year 1925.
explanation.walkthrough: '1925' looks like a year but is two clue numbers: the answers at 19 and 25, ACTING EXIT, run together.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight trace or touch, a hint of flavour.

clue.text: Film covering team's departure

indicators.note: covering means the film title goes around the team

parts.note: ET is the Spielberg film
XI, eleven, is a football or cricket team

explanation.surface: A film about a team leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit is a way out or a leaving.

clue.text: Nauseating refusal by Indian to swap sides after he departed

indicators.note: after puts the refusal and the Indian after the abbreviation for he departed

parts.note: ob., from Latin obiit, means he died
no is a refusal

indicators.note: to swap says the two end letters of the people's name trade places, this half bringing the last one to the front
sides names the two end letters of the people's name, the first of which is sent to the far end

parts.note: the Sioux are a Native American people

explanation.surface: A sickening refusal by an Indian to defect after a man walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: SIOUX with its outer letters swapped gives XIOUS.

clue.text: Discover driver being instructed to leave Paris

indicators.note: to leave means the learner letter departs from the surname

parts.note: Paris Hilton is an American celebrity heiress
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Finding out that a learner driver is being told to get out of Paris.

explanation.definitionFit: To hit on an idea is to discover or come upon it.

clue.text: Group of players footballers are reluctant to play with?

definitions.text: footballers are reluctant to play with?
definitions.meaning: read as two words, a goal without netting, which players would not want

explanation.surface: A team that footballers would rather not join.

clue.text: Hear education minister, with nothing to lose, attempt to deceive Secretary-General

parts.note: a court hears, or tries, a case

indicators.note: to lose means the minister's name gives up the zero letter

parts.note: Michael Gove was the UK Education Secretary from 2010 to 2014
O is zero, or nothing
a lie is an attempt to deceive

explanation.surface: A minister is heard trying to mislead the UN chief, with nothing to lose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' is the judicial sense, to try a case. Michael Gove was Britain's education minister at the time.
